output.brief: What is going on: the VX rejects are not caused by the six new operators or by the Arnholt resin on its own. They come from Arnholt resin being dried in dryer D5, which has been running wet (dew point about -16 to -19 C instead of -40 C) since late July. Second shift is high only because it runs on Press 5, and the new hires reject at the same rate as experienced operators on the same press and resin. Arnholt run through Press 7 or a portable dryer at -40 C runs at about 0.8%, the normal baseline. Quillan resin through the same D5 is fine at 0.9%, so the dryer alone is not the whole story. How sure: fairly confident about the operator and resin conclusions. The link from D5 moisture to rejects is strong but rests on one trial lot. Whether the north annex storage makes Arnholt wetter is not yet tested, because all Arnholt samples came from the annex. What to do this week: repair D5 (heater, desiccant), restore its original alarm limit, and keep Arnholt off D5 until it is verified. Add a moisture check for each VX resin lot. Do not put the six operators on improvement plans. Moving stock out of the annex can wait until it is tested.
